summary: Explains using a Windows scheduled task to bypass WinRM restrictions, with an example that creates a self-deleting task via win_scheduled_task and waits for it with win_scheduled_task_stat. Modules were added/updated in Ansible 2.5.
questions: How can I get around WinRM restrictions when a command fails remotely?
How do I run a one-off script as SYSTEM through a scheduled task with Ansible?
How do I wait for a Windows scheduled task to finish in a playbook?
How do I make a scheduled task delete itself after it runs?

answer_card.title: Running a command via a scheduled task to bypass WinRM limits
answer_card.answer_md:
```yaml
- win_scheduled_task:
    name: adhoc-task
    username: SYSTEM
    actions:
    - path: PowerShell.exe
      arguments: New-Item -Path C:\temp\test -ItemType Directory
    - path: cmd.exe           # remove to keep the task
      arguments: /c schtasks.exe /Delete /TN "adhoc-task" /F
    triggers:
    - type: registration

- win_scheduled_task_stat:
    name: adhoc-task
  register: task_stat
  until: (task_stat.state is defined and task_stat.state.status != "TASK_STATE_RUNNING") or (task_stat.task_exists == False)
  retries: 12
  delay: 10
```

These modules need Ansible 2.5 or newer.
